Scarlet-orange sharp little triangular flowers in dozens, each one needle-pointed and hot as an ember (masdevallia), packed along the near end of a single bare limb, pale roots clamped flat to the wet dark bark, nothing else in flower on the whole length of wood.

Dozens of tiny bright egg-yellow stars strung along one long arching spray (oncidium), the whole sweep hanging out over open air, pale roots gripping a bare-bark knob at the base so the spray curves away from the limb and floats unsupported over the drop below.

Heavy waxy ivory-cream flowers freckled deep maroon (stanhopea), three of them hanging straight down out of the underside of a soaking moss pad wedged into a fork, the blooms dangling below the wood like weighted pendulums while grey-green tillandsia tufts bristle above.

Pure white wide flat flowers with small gold middles, six of them turned the same way toward the camera (phalaenopsis), all on one arching stem, pale roots spread flat over bare bark and clamped down, a curtain of hanging moss filling the dark gap behind them.

Deep blue-violet flat wide flowers each as wide across as the limb they sit on is thick, each one carrying a fine chequered pattern (vanda), pale roots clamped over the top of the limb beside a stiff ring of red-and-green banded leaves holding standing water in the middle (bromeliad).

Bright egg-yellow flowers packed so close along the full length of a mossy limb (maxillaria) that the whole limb reads as one solid band of yellow from tip to tip, pale roots wedged under every flake of loose bark, filmy fern in thin translucent sheets draping the underside.

Hanging chains of pure white flowers each with a gold-brown middle (coelogyne), dropping straight down a trunk in two long curtains, pale roots spread flat over the bark and clamped down, liverwort quilted flat in dark green patches all around the root mass.

Big waxy lemon-yellow triangular flowers, one to a stem (lycaste), wedged into a crack in the bark, pale roots pushed deep into the gap, liverwort in a dark quilted sheet all round the base, the yellow blooms standing upright against near-black wet wood.

Tight round clusters of small orange-red flowers on thin wiry stems (epidendrum), the stems leaning out over a bromeliad's pool of standing water below, pale roots clamped over the top of the limb just behind the fork, the red-and-green banded leaves framing the stems from beneath.

Cream-white flowers heavily blotched chestnut-red (odontoglossum), spilling out of a fork in three short sprays, pale roots packed into soaking moss in the fork's angle, silver-spotted begonia leaves fanning out beneath them and catching every drop of condensation.

Waxy apple-green flowers with bright red middles on two long arching stems (cymbidium), the stems curving out over glossy scarlet heart-shaped anthurium leaves below, pale roots spread flat over bare bark and clamped down on the upper side of a thick horizontal limb.

Small white flowers tipped purple in loose arching sprays (dendrobium), the sprays lifting above the broad flat fronds of a tree fern that crowds the same fork, pale roots wedged into a dense pad of soaking moss, the purple tips catching what flat light filters through the canopy above.

Deep blue-violet chequered flowers each as wide across as the limb they sit on is thick (vanda), ranked all the way up the flank of a trunk in a staggered line of six plants, pale roots clamped flat to the bark between each one, a wiry grey-green tillandsia tuft wedged between every pair of plants.

A single limb carrying four orchid plants: big waxy lemon-yellow triangular flowers (lycaste) open at the near end, the other three — white, scarlet-orange and cream — all out of flower and showing only dark leaves and pale roots pressed flat to the bark the full length of the wood.

One big ruffled deep magenta-purple flower (cattleya), one flower only, its pale roots clamped over the top of a mossy limb, the rest of the frame filled with dark wet bark, dripping filmy fern and pale grey-green lichen so the single bloom reads like a shout in a silent room.

Dozens of tiny bright egg-yellow stars (oncidium) arching out of a moss pad at the base of a trunk, the spray sweeping upward and then falling back in a long loose arc, stiff red-and-green banded bromeliad leaves crowding the trunk below and propping standing water just under the roots.

Hot scarlet-orange triangular flowers in dozens (masdevallia), ranked up the shaded flank of a fallen trunk, each plant's pale roots clamped flat to the bark, pale grey-green lichen spreading between the root pads in irregular islands, no other flower anywhere on the wood.

Deep blue-violet wide flat chequered flowers (vanda) spilling out of a high fork, pale roots clamped over the top of each arm of the fork, grey-green tillandsia tufts wedged into the moss beside them, the flowers hanging outward over open air and turning their flat faces downward.

Small bright egg-yellow flowers packed close along the bark in a short dense row (maxillaria) beside hanging chains of pure white gold-centred flowers (coelogyne) dropping off the same limb's underside, two root masses pressed flat to the wood within a hand's width of each other.

Tight round clusters of small orange-red flowers on thin wiry stems (epidendrum), crowded along the top of a mossy limb, pale roots spread flat over the moss and clamped down, silver-spotted begonia leaves spilling from the fork below and pressing up against the underside of the limb.

Big soft rose-purple flowers, two of them open this morning and already beginning to close (sobralia), arching out over open air on stiff upright stems, pale roots wedged into a thick pad of soaking moss on the trunk's flank, a curtain of hanging moss dark and dripping just behind.

Pure white wide flat flowers with gold middles (phalaenopsis) hanging straight down off the underside of a limb on one long arching stem, pale roots pressed flat to the bark above, cream-white flowers heavily blotched chestnut-red (odontoglossum) crowding the top of the same limb just beside them.

Deep blue-violet flat wide chequered flowers (vanda) clamped over the top of a thick limb by pale roots spread flat across bare bark, hot scarlet-orange sharp little triangular flowers (masdevallia) hanging straight down off the underside of the same limb just past the fork, nothing else on the wood.

Big waxy lemon-yellow triangular flowers (lycaste) and dozens of tiny bright egg-yellow stars on a long arching spray (oncidium) sharing one fork, the triangular flowers upright and the spray bowing out over the drop, pale roots of both plants packed into the same soaking moss pad in the fork's angle.

Small white flowers tipped purple in arching sprays (dendrobium) and tight round clusters of small orange-red flowers on thin wiry stems (epidendrum) ranked side by side up the flank of a trunk, pale roots of both clamped flat to the bark, liverwort in a dark flat sheet filling every gap between the root pads.
